        <style>
          .quarto-container, .page-columns, .main-container {
            max-width: 100% !important;
          }
        </style>



Key choices: code-fold: true hides code by default (biologist audience), toc: true for navigation, embed-resources: true for self-contained HTML.




Section 1: Introduction


Content: Plain text (no code). Explain:


    

  • The experiment: Yentur et al. 2025 treated human dorsal forebrain organoids with valproic acid (VPA), an anti-epileptic drug and known teratogen linked to neural tube defects and autism
    • 

  • Two iPSC donor lines (BIONi010-C and KOLF2.1J), two conditions (CTRL vs VPA), ~26,500 cells total
    • 

  • What this analysis will cover: visualization, composition changes, differential gene expression, pathway analysis
    • 

  • Data source: CELLxGENE (dataset ID 3a8aec06-3309-4d37-b75d-c59f5f6d55a6)
    • 





Section 2: Setup and Data Loading


Packages: SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, ggplot2, dplyr, tidyr, DT, patchwork, plotly, edgeR, limma, clusterProfiler, org.Hs.eg.db, fgsea, msigdbr, ComplexHeatmap, pheatmap, viridis, RColorBrewer, ggrepel, scales, here, Matrix, glue


Code:


    

  • Load all libraries
    • 

  • sce <- readRDS(here::here("analysis", "vpa_organoids_sce.rds"))
    • 

  • Print basic dimensions: `r ncol(sce)` cells, `r nrow(sce)` genes
    • 

  • Define a helper function to make gene symbols clickable (link to GeneCards: https://www.genecards.org/cgi-bin/carddisp.pl?gene=SYMBOL)
    • 

  • Define a color palette for cell types (consistent throughout the document)
    • 

  • Note: explain that feature_name in rowData maps ENSG IDs to gene symbols where available (21,336 of 27,986 genes have symbols)
    • 



Explanatory text: "We begin by loading the preprocessed dataset. The data was originally published as an h5ad file on CELLxGENE and has been converted to R's SingleCellExperiment format. The expression values are log-normalized (natural log of counts plus one), and the authors have already assigned cell type labels and computed a UMAP embedding."




Section 3: Experimental Design Overview


Code:


    

  • Cross-tabulation table of condition x donor_id (with knitr::kable)
    • 

  • Cross-tabulation of condition x cell_type
    • 

  • Note the paired design: every donor has both conditions
    • 



Explanatory text: "The experiment uses a paired design: both iPSC donor lines were subjected to both control and VPA conditions. This pairing is statistically powerful because it allows us to separate the effect of VPA from donor-to-donor variation."




Section 4: UMAP Visualizations


Code (using ggplot2 directly on extracted UMAP coordinates + colData):


    

  1. UMAP colored by cell type (the 5-level cell_type)
    2. 

  2. UMAP colored by condition (CTRL vs VPA) -- use split facets
    3. 

  3. UMAP colored by author_cell_type (9-level, more detailed)
    4. 

  4. UMAP colored by donor_id
    5. 

  5. UMAP colored by cell_phase (cell cycle)
    6. 

  6. UMAP split by condition, colored by cell type (side by side using facet_wrap)
    7. 



Use plotly::ggplotly() for at least the main cell-type UMAP so biologists can hover over points.


Explanatory text: "UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a dimensionality reduction method that places similar cells near each other. Each dot is one cell. These visualizations let us see the overall structure of the data and how conditions differ."




Section 5: Cell Type Composition Analysis


This is where the story gets interesting -- VPA dramatically shifts cell composition.


Code:


    

  1. Stacked bar chart: proportion of each cell type within CTRL vs VPA
    2. 

  2. Same broken down by donor (4 bars: CTRL-donor1, CTRL-donor2, VPA-donor1, VPA-donor2)
    3. 

  3. Table with exact numbers and percentages
    4. 

  4. A dot plot or paired-line plot showing the proportion shift per donor (to show the paired design)
    5. 

  5. Optional: Fisher's exact or chi-squared test for composition differences (or simple proportion comparison)
    6. 



Key finding to highlight: Progenitors increase from ~17% to ~42%, cortical neurons decrease from ~76% to ~43%. This is consistent with VPA inhibiting neuronal differentiation.


Explanatory text: "Before looking at which genes change, we first ask: does VPA change the proportions of cell types? This is called a 'compositional analysis.' A shift in cell type proportions can be as biologically meaningful as changes in gene expression within a given cell type."




Section 6: Differential Expression Analysis


6a: Pseudobulk Aggregation


Code:


    

  • Back-transform log-normalized data: round(expm1(X)) to get approximate counts
    • 

  • Aggregate (sum) per donor x condition x cell_type (this creates pseudobulk samples)
    • 

  • This gives us, for each cell type, 4 pseudobulk samples: 2 CTRL (one per donor) + 2 VPA (one per donor)
    • 

  • Store as a DGEList (edgeR)
    • 



Explanatory text: "Single-cell DE analysis is most reliable when cells are first grouped ('pseudobulked') by biological replicate. This avoids the statistical pitfall of treating thousands of cells from the same sample as independent observations. We sum the expression counts for each gene across all cells of a given type within each donor-condition combination, producing four 'pseudobulk' samples per cell type."


Important caveat to state: With only 2 donors per condition, statistical power is limited. Results should be interpreted as exploratory.


6b: DE with limma-voom (per cell type)


Code:


    

  • For each major cell type (at minimum: progenitor cell, cerebral cortex neuron, neuronal-restricted precursor):
      

    • Create design matrix with ~donor_id + condition (paired design)
      • 

    • Filter low-expression genes using edgeR::filterByExpr()
      • 

    • edgeR::calcNormFactors()
      • 

    • limma::voom() -> limma::lmFit() -> limma::eBayes()
      • 

    • Extract results with limma::topTable(coef = "conditionVPA", number = Inf)
      • 

    

    • 

  • Combine results across cell types
    • 



6c: Visualization of DE Results


Code:


    

  1. Volcano plots per cell type (ggplot2, highlight top genes with ggrepel)
    2. 

  2. Summary table: number of DE genes (FDR < 0.05) up/down per cell type
    3. 

  3. Interactive table (DT::datatable) of top DE genes per cell type, with clickable gene symbols linking to GeneCards
    4. 

  4. Heatmap of top DE genes across pseudobulk samples (ComplexHeatmap or pheatmap)
    5. 



Explanatory text: "A volcano plot shows each gene's statistical significance (y-axis) against its fold change (x-axis). Genes in the upper-left are significantly downregulated by VPA; genes in the upper-right are significantly upregulated."




Section 7: Pathway / Gene Set Enrichment Analysis


Code:


    

  • Use fgsea with msigdbr gene sets (Hallmark, GO BP, KEGG)
    • 

  • Run GSEA on the ranked gene list (ranked by t-statistic from limma) for each cell type
    • 

  • Alternatively/additionally: clusterProfiler::enrichGO() on significant DE genes (over-representation analysis)
    • 

  • Dot plot / bar plot of top enriched pathways
    • 

  • Compare enriched pathways across cell types
    • 



Explanatory text: "Individual gene changes can be hard to interpret. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) asks whether groups of functionally related genes tend to be coordinately up- or down-regulated. This reveals the biological processes affected by VPA."




Section 8: Marker Genes and Known Biology


Code:


    

  • Violin plots or dot plots of known VPA-response genes (e.g., HDAC targets, Wnt pathway, Notch pathway genes) split by condition
    • 

  • Dot plot of cell-type marker genes by condition (to verify cell type annotations and see if markers shift)
    • 

  • Feature plots (UMAP colored by expression) for top DE genes
    • 



Explanatory text: "We examine specific genes of known biological relevance. VPA is a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor, so we expect changes in genes regulated by histone acetylation. We also check markers of neural progenitor identity and neuronal differentiation."




Section 9: Draft Results Section


Plain text (dynamically generated with inline R) summarizing:


    

  • Cell composition changes with exact numbers
    • 

  • Number of DE genes per cell type
    • 

  • Key pathways
    • 

  • Top genes
    • 





Section 10: Draft Methods Section


Plain text describing:


    

  • Data source and accession
    • 

  • Software versions (pulled from sessionInfo)
    • 

  • Statistical methods (pseudobulk, limma-voom, paired design, FDR correction)
    • 

  • Pathway analysis methods
    • 





Section 11: Session Info


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Session Info
```{r}
#| label: session-info
#| echo: false
#| comment: ""
sessioninfo::session_info(info = "all")



:::



---

### Potential Challenges and Mitigations

1. **No raw counts available**: The assay contains `log1p`-normalized data. Using `expm1()` to back-transform and then rounding gives approximate counts. This is imperfect but standard practice when raw counts are unavailable from CELLxGENE h5ad files. The pseudobulk summation over hundreds/thousands of cells smooths out rounding errors.

2. **Only 2 biological replicates (donors)**: With n=2 per group, limma-voom's empirical Bayes shrinkage helps, and the paired design (blocking on donor) recovers one degree of freedom. Still, we should be explicit that results are exploratory and use moderate significance thresholds. The document should state this limitation clearly.

3. **6,650 genes lack gene symbols**: These are mostly non-coding RNAs. We should filter to protein-coding genes for most analyses (using `feature_biotype` or simply filtering for genes with symbols in `feature_name`).

4. **Large dense matrix (238 MB RDS)**: Loading and back-transforming the full dense matrix will use substantial memory. Consider working on subsets (per cell type) rather than the whole matrix at once.

5. **Cajal-Retzius cells and "unknown" are small groups**: CR cells have only 287 total (194 CTRL, 93 VPA) and "unknown" has 463. Pseudobulk with only ~45-100 cells per donor-condition may be unreliable. Consider excluding these from cell-type-specific DE or noting the caveat.

### Packages to Install

None of the currently-unavailable packages (scater, scran, Seurat, MAST, muscat, dittoSeq) are needed for this plan. Everything can be accomplished with the installed packages: SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, edgeR, limma, ggplot2, plotly, patchwork, DT, ComplexHeatmap, pheatmap, clusterProfiler, enrichplot, org.Hs.eg.db, fgsea, msigdbr, viridis, RColorBrewer, ggrepel, dplyr, tidyr, Matrix, scales, glue, here, knitr, sessioninfo.

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/home/steve/github/recount3SRP150473/analysis/vpa_organoids_sce.rds` - The input SCE object; understanding its structure (log1p-normalized assay "X", colData columns, reducedDims "X_umap", rowData with feature_name) is essential
- `/home/steve/github/recount3SRP150473/analysis/00_find_cellxgene_dataset.R` - Reference for how the data was downloaded and converted; confirms the h5ad-to-SCE pipeline
- `/home/steve/.claude/CLAUDE.md` - User's Quarto/R conventions that must be followed throughout (YAML header, code block labels, dplyr::filter, inline R, session info format, clickable gene links, etc.)

# Plan: Quarto Analysis of Control vs VPA-Treated Organoid scRNA-seq

## Context

We downloaded a 2-condition scRNA-seq dataset (Yentür et al. 2025, bioRxiv) from CELLxGENE: human dorsal forebrain organoids, control vs VPA-treated, 26,499 cells. The purpose is to demo LLM-assisted analysis on a dataset the LLM hasn't seen extensively. The audience is biologists, so explanatory text is needed at each step.

## Output File

`analysis/02_ctrl_vs_vpa_analysis.qmd` → self-contained HTML

## Data Summary

- Input: `analysis/vpa_organoids_sce.rds` (SingleCellExperiment, 27,986 genes × 26,499 cells)
- Assay `"X"`: log1p-normalized expression (no raw counts available)
- `condition`: CTRL (12,995) vs VPA (13,504)
- `cell_type`: 5 types (progenitor, neuronal-restricted precursor, Cajal-Retzius, cerebral cortex neuron, unknown)
- `donor_id`: 2 donors (paired design — each donor has both conditions)
- `batch`, `cell_phase` available
- UMAP already computed in `reducedDims(sce, "X_umap")`

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Use existing annotations/UMAP** from the original authors — don't recompute
2. **Pseudobulk DE with limma-voom** (paired design blocking on donor): `expm1()` to back-transform, sum per donor×condition×cell_type, then edgeR/limma pipeline
3. **Caveat**: only 2 donors per condition — results are exploratory; state this clearly
4. **code-fold: true** — hide code by default for biologist audience
5. **All packages already installed** — no new installs needed

## Document Sections

### 1. YAML Header
- Follow CLAUDE.md conventions (author, date, page-layout: full, embed-resources, CSS override)
- Add: toc: true, code-fold: true, code-summary: "Show code"

### 2. Introduction (text only)
- What the experiment is (VPA = HDAC inhibitor, teratogen linked to autism)
- Paired design: 2 donors × 2 conditions
- What the analysis covers

### 3. Setup & Data Loading
- Load packages: SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, edgeR, limma, ggplot2, plotly, patchwork, DT, dplyr, tidyr, ggrepel, fgsea, msigdbr, pheatmap, here, glue, scales
- Load SCE, print dims with inline R
- Define color palettes for cell types and conditions
- Helper: clickable gene symbol links to GeneCards

### 4. Experimental Design Overview
- Cross-tabulation tables: condition × donor_id, condition × cell_type
- Explain paired design in plain English

### 5. UMAP Visualizations
- UMAP colored by: cell_type, condition, donor_id, cell_phase
- Side-by-side UMAP split by condition (facet_wrap)
- At least one interactive plotly UMAP
- Explain what UMAP is for biologists

### 6. Cell Type Composition Analysis
- Stacked bar chart: cell type proportions per condition
- Broken down by donor (4 bars) to show consistency
- Table with exact numbers/percentages
- Highlight: progenitors increase, neurons decrease under VPA

### 7. Differential Expression (per cell type)
#### 7a. Pseudobulk aggregation
- Back-transform: `round(expm1(assay(sce, "X")))` → approximate counts
- Sum per donor × condition × cell_type → DGEList
- Explain pseudobulk rationale for biologists

#### 7b. limma-voom DE
- For each major cell type (progenitor, cortex neuron, neuronal-restricted precursor):
  - Design: `~donor_id + condition` (paired)
  - filterByExpr → calcNormFactors → voom → lmFit → eBayes → topTable
- Skip Cajal-Retzius and unknown (too few cells per donor)
- Combine results

#### 7c. DE Visualization
- Volcano plots per cell type (ggrepel for top genes)
- Summary table: # DE genes up/down per cell type (FDR < 0.05)
- Interactive DT table of top DE genes with clickable gene symbols
- Heatmap of top DE genes across pseudobulk samples

### 8. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
- fgsea with msigdbr Hallmark + GO BP gene sets
- Rank genes by limma t-statistic per cell type
- Dot plot of top enriched pathways
- Explain GSEA concept for biologists

### 9. Known Biology Check
- Violin plots of known VPA-response / neural development genes split by condition and cell type
- Feature plots (UMAP colored by expression) for top DE genes

### 10. Draft Results
- Dynamically generated text using inline R
- Cell composition shifts, # DE genes, key pathways, top genes

### 11. Draft Methods
- Data source, software versions, statistical methods, pathway analysis

### 12. Session Info
- Collapsible callout per CLAUDE.md convention

## Packages (all installed)
edgeR, limma, SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, ggplot2, plotly, patchwork, DT, dplyr, tidyr, ggrepel, fgsea, msigdbr, pheatmap, scales, glue, here, Matrix, sessioninfo, viridis

## Known Risks
1. **No raw counts**: back-transforming log1p is approximate but standard for CELLxGENE data; pseudobulk summation smooths rounding errors
2. **n=2 donors**: limited power; use empirical Bayes shrinkage; state results are exploratory
3. **Small cell groups**: Cajal-Retzius (287 cells) and unknown (463) — skip for cell-type-specific DE
4. **Memory**: 238 MB dense matrix; work per cell type where possible

## Verification
1. `quarto render analysis/02_ctrl_vs_vpa_analysis.qmd` should produce self-contained HTML
2. Check UMAP plots show expected clustering
3. Check DE tables have clickable gene links
4. Check Results/Methods drafts use inline R (not hardcoded numbers)
5. Verify HTML is self-contained (open in browser without network)

# Plan: Quarto Analysis of Control vs VPA-Treated Organoid scRNA-seq

## Context

We downloaded a 2-condition scRNA-seq dataset (Yentür et al. 2025, bioRxiv) from CELLxGENE: human dorsal forebrain organoids, control vs VPA-treated, 26,499 cells. The purpose is to demo LLM-assisted analysis on a dataset the LLM hasn't seen extensively. The audience is biologists, so explanatory text is needed at each step.

## Output File

`analysis/02_ctrl_vs_vpa_analysis.qmd` → self-contained HTML

## Data Summary

- Input: `analysis/vpa_organoids_sce.rds` (SingleCellExperiment, 27,986 genes × 26,499 cells)
- Assay `"X"`: log1p-normalized expression (no raw counts available)
- `condition`: CTRL (12,995) vs VPA (13,504)
- `cell_type`: 5 types (progenitor, neuronal-restricted precursor, Cajal-Retzius, cerebral cortex neuron, unknown)
- `donor_id`: 2 donors (paired design — each donor has both conditions)
- `batch`, `cell_phase` available
- UMAP already computed in `reducedDims(sce, "X_umap")`

## Key Design Decisions

1. **Use existing annotations/UMAP** from the original authors — don't recompute
2. **Pseudobulk DE with limma-voom** (paired design blocking on donor): `expm1()` to back-transform, sum per donor×condition×cell_type, then edgeR/limma pipeline
3. **Caveat**: only 2 donors per condition — results are exploratory; state this clearly
4. **code-fold: true** — hide code by default for biologist audience
5. **All packages already installed** — no new installs needed

## Document Sections

### 1. YAML Header
- Follow CLAUDE.md conventions (author, date, page-layout: full, embed-resources, CSS override)
- Add: toc: true, code-fold: true, code-summary: "Show code"

### 2. Introduction (text only)
- What the experiment is (VPA = HDAC inhibitor, teratogen linked to autism)
- Paired design: 2 donors × 2 conditions
- What the analysis covers

### 3. Setup & Data Loading
- Load packages: SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, edgeR, limma, ggplot2, plotly, patchwork, DT, dplyr, tidyr, ggrepel, fgsea, msigdbr, pheatmap, here, glue, scales
- Load SCE, print dims with inline R
- Define color palettes for cell types and conditions
- Helper: clickable gene symbol links to GeneCards

### 4. Experimental Design Overview
- Cross-tabulation tables: condition × donor_id, condition × cell_type
- Explain paired design in plain English

### 5. UMAP Visualizations
- UMAP colored by: cell_type, condition, donor_id, cell_phase
- Side-by-side UMAP split by condition (facet_wrap)
- At least one interactive plotly UMAP
- Explain what UMAP is for biologists

### 6. Cell Type Composition Analysis
- Stacked bar chart: cell type proportions per condition
- Broken down by donor (4 bars) to show consistency
- Table with exact numbers/percentages
- Highlight: progenitors increase, neurons decrease under VPA

### 7. Differential Expression (per cell type)
#### 7a. Pseudobulk aggregation
- Back-transform: `round(expm1(assay(sce, "X")))` → approximate counts
- Sum per donor × condition × cell_type → DGEList
- Explain pseudobulk rationale for biologists

#### 7b. limma-voom DE
- For each major cell type (progenitor, cortex neuron, neuronal-restricted precursor):
  - Design: `~donor_id + condition` (paired)
  - filterByExpr → calcNormFactors → voom → lmFit → eBayes → topTable
- Skip Cajal-Retzius and unknown (too few cells per donor)
- Combine results

#### 7c. DE Visualization
- Volcano plots per cell type (ggrepel for top genes)
- Summary table: # DE genes up/down per cell type (FDR < 0.05)
- Interactive DT table of top DE genes with clickable gene symbols
- Heatmap of top DE genes across pseudobulk samples

### 8. Gene Set Enrichment Analysis
- fgsea with msigdbr Hallmark + GO BP gene sets
- Rank genes by limma t-statistic per cell type
- Dot plot of top enriched pathways
- Explain GSEA concept for biologists

### 9. Known Biology Check
- Violin plots of known VPA-response / neural development genes split by condition and cell type
- Feature plots (UMAP colored by expression) for top DE genes

### 10. Draft Results
- Dynamically generated text using inline R
- Cell composition shifts, # DE genes, key pathways, top genes

### 11. Draft Methods
- Data source, software versions, statistical methods, pathway analysis

### 12. Session Info
- Collapsible callout per CLAUDE.md convention

## Packages (all installed)
edgeR, limma, SingleCellExperiment, SummarizedExperiment, ggplot2, plotly, patchwork, DT, dplyr, tidyr, ggrepel, fgsea, msigdbr, pheatmap, scales, glue, here, Matrix, sessioninfo, viridis

## Known Risks
1. **No raw counts**: back-transforming log1p is approximate but standard for CELLxGENE data; pseudobulk summation smooths rounding errors
2. **n=2 donors**: limited power; use empirical Bayes shrinkage; state results are exploratory
3. **Small cell groups**: Cajal-Retzius (287 cells) and unknown (463) — skip for cell-type-specific DE
4. **Memory**: 238 MB dense matrix; work per cell type where possible

# Find a 2-condition scRNA-seq dataset on CELLxGENE
# that is small and not widely used in tutorials

# install.packages("BiocManager")
# BiocManager::install("cellxgenedp")

library(cellxgenedp)
library(dplyr)

db <- db(overwrite = FALSE)

# See what diseases are available
facets(db, "disease")

# Look at all datasets with their metadata
ds <- datasets(db)
colnames(ds)

# Find datasets that have a disease (not just "normal")
# and are relatively small (< 50K cells)
ds_small <- ds |>
  dplyr::filter(
    cell_count < 50000,
    cell_count > 1000
  )

nrow(ds_small)

# Check which of these have disease annotations
ds_small |>
  select(dataset_id, title, cell_count, disease, organism, assay) |>
  print(n = 30)

# ---- download-vpa-organoids ----
# Control vs VPA-treated dorsal forebrain organoids (26,499 cells)
vpa_dataset_id <- "3a8aec06-3309-4d37-b75d-c59f5f6d55a6" # selected from human examinatino ofds_small

vpa_file <- ds |>
  dplyr::filter(dataset_id == vpa_dataset_id) |>
  left_join(files(db), by = "dataset_id") |>
  dplyr::filter(filetype == "H5AD")

local_h5ad <- files_download(vpa_file, dry.run = FALSE)
cat("Downloaded to:", local_h5ad, "\n")

# Convert to SingleCellExperiment
# BiocManager::install("zellkonverter")
library(zellkonverter)
sce <- readH5AD(local_h5ad, use_hdf5 = TRUE, reader = "R")
sce
dim(sce)
library(SummarizedExperiment)
colnames(colData(sce))
table(colData(sce)$condition)

# Load data into memory (from HDF5-backed) so it can be saved as RDS
assay(sce, "X") <- as.matrix(assay(sce, "X"))
saveRDS(sce, here::here("analysis", "vpa_organoids_sce.rds"))

## Introduction

Valproic acid (VPA) is a widely prescribed antiepileptic drug that also acts as a
**histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor**. Prenatal exposure to VPA is an established
teratogen and has been linked to increased risk of autism spectrum disorder and other
neurodevelopmental conditions.

This analysis examines single-cell RNA-seq data from
[Yentür et al. (2025, bioRxiv)](https://doi.org/10.1101/2025.01.09.632137),
comparing **control** vs **VPA-treated** human dorsal forebrain organoids.
The dataset was obtained from
[CELLxGENE](https://cellxgene.cziscience.com/) and contains 26,499 cells across
5 annotated cell types.

**Experimental design**: 2 donors, each contributing organoids to both control and
VPA conditions (a paired design). Because we have only 2 biological replicates per
condition, all differential expression results should be considered **exploratory**.

**What this analysis covers**:

1. Visualization of cell populations (UMAP)
2. Cell type composition changes under VPA
3. Pseudobulk differential expression per cell type (limma-voom, paired design)
4. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA with Hallmark and GO gene sets)
5. Expression of known VPA-response and neural development genes

## Experimental Design Overview

The experiment uses a **paired design**: each donor contributes cells to both
conditions. This lets us account for donor-to-donor variability when testing
for VPA effects.

```{r}

table(sce$condition, sce$donor_id)

cat("\nCells per condition × cell type:\n")
table(sce$condition, sce$cell_type)
```

  table(Condition = sce$condition, Donor = sce$donor_id, CellType = sce$cell_type)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(Freq > 0) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = Condition, values_from = Freq, values_fill = 0)

DT::datatable(design_df, caption = "Cell counts by donor, condition, and cell type",
              options = list(pageLength = 20))

## UMAP Visualizations

UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection) is a dimensionality reduction
technique that projects high-dimensional gene expression data into 2D for
visualization. Cells that are close together on the UMAP have similar expression
profiles. The UMAP coordinates here were computed by the original study authors.

```{r}

  UMAP1     = reducedDim(sce, "X_umap")[, 1],
  UMAP2     = reducedDim(sce, "X_umap")[, 2],
  cell_type = sce$cell_type,
  condition = sce$condition,
  donor_id  = sce$donor_id,
  cell_phase = sce$cell_phase
)
```

## Cell Type Composition Analysis

A key question in case-control scRNA-seq studies is whether the **proportions** of
cell types shift between conditions. Changes in composition can reflect altered
differentiation, proliferation, or survival.

```{r}
#| label: composition-data
comp_df <- as.data.frame(table(
  condition = sce$condition,
  cell_type = sce$cell_type,
  donor_id  = sce$donor_id
))

# Compute proportions within each condition × donor
comp_df <- comp_df |>
  group_by(condition, donor_id) |>
  mutate(
    total = sum(Freq),
    proportion = Freq / total
  ) |>
  ungroup()
```

### Stacked Bar Chart

#| fig-width: 10

  group_by(condition, cell_type) |>
  summarize(Freq = sum(Freq), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  mutate(proportion = Freq / sum(Freq)) |>
  ungroup()

ggplot(comp_cond, aes(condition, proportion, fill = cell_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.6) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = cell_type_colors) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format()) +
  labs(
    title = "Cell type composition by condition",

  )

## Differential Expression Analysis

### Pseudobulk Aggregation

Single-cell DE analysis requires careful statistical treatment. Simply treating
each cell as an independent replicate inflates false positives because cells from
the same donor are correlated. The **pseudobulk** approach addresses this by
summing expression counts across all cells of a given type within each biological
replicate (donor × condition), then applying bulk RNA-seq statistical methods.

Since the CELLxGENE data provides log1p-normalized values rather than raw counts,
we back-transform with `expm1()` and round to approximate integer counts. This is
a standard workaround and the pseudobulk summation over thousands of cells smooths
rounding artifacts.

```{r}
#| label: pseudobulk-aggregation
#| message: false
# Back-transform log1p to approximate counts
# Work per cell type to manage memory
cell_types_for_de <- c(
  "progenitor",
  "cerebral cortex neuron",
  "neuronal-restricted precursor"
)

# Create pseudobulk samples
make_pseudobulk <- function(sce, cell_type_name) {
  idx <- which(sce$cell_type == cell_type_name)
  sub <- sce[, idx]

  # Define groups
  groups <- paste(sub$condition, sub$donor_id, sep = "_")
  group_levels <- unique(groups)

  # Sum approximate counts per group
  mat <- assay(sub, "X")
  pb <- do.call(cbind, lapply(group_levels, function(g) {
    cells <- which(groups == g)
    if (length(cells) == 1) {
      round(expm1(mat[, cells, drop = FALSE]))
    } else {
      Matrix::rowSums(round(expm1(mat[, cells, drop = FALSE])))
    }
  }))
  colnames(pb) <- group_levels

  # Sample metadata
  sample_info <- data.frame(
    sample    = group_levels,
    condition = sub("^(CTRL|VPA)_.*$", "\\1", group_levels),
    donor_id  = sub("^(CTRL|VPA)_", "", group_levels),
    n_cells   = as.integer(table(groups)[group_levels]),
    row.names = group_levels
  )

  list(counts = as.matrix(pb), sample_info = sample_info)
}

pseudobulk_list <- lapply(
  setNames(cell_types_for_de, cell_types_for_de),
  function(ct) make_pseudobulk(sce, ct)
)

# Show sample sizes
for (ct in names(pseudobulk_list)) {
  cat("\n", ct, ":\n")
  print(pseudobulk_list[[ct]]$sample_info[, c("sample", "condition", "n_cells")])
}
```

### limma-voom Differential Expression

We use **limma-voom** with a paired design formula `~donor_id + condition` to
test for VPA effects while blocking on donor variability. The **empirical Bayes**
shrinkage in limma is especially valuable with small sample sizes, as it borrows
information across genes to stabilize variance estimates.

**Important caveat**: With only 2 donors per condition, statistical power is
limited. These results identify candidate genes for follow-up but should not be
treated as definitive.

```{r}
#| label: limma-voom-de
#| message: false
#| warning: false
run_limma_voom <- function(pb, cell_type_name) {
  counts <- pb$counts
  info   <- pb$sample_info

  # Create DGEList
  y <- DGEList(counts = counts, samples = info)

  # Filter lowly expressed genes
  keep <- filterByExpr(y, group = info$condition)
  y <- y[keep, , keep.lib.sizes = FALSE]

  # Normalize
  y <- calcNormFactors(y)

  # Design matrix (paired)
  design <- model.matrix(~donor_id + condition, data = info)

  # voom transformation
  v <- voom(y, design, plot = FALSE)

  # Fit
  fit <- lmFit(v, design)
  fit <- eBayes(fit)

  # Extract results for VPA effect
  # The coefficient name depends on the factor levels
  coef_name <- grep("condition", colnames(coef(fit)), value = TRUE)

  tt <- topTable(fit, coef = coef_name, number = Inf, sort.by = "none")
  tt$gene <- rownames(tt)
  tt$cell_type <- cell_type_name
  tt
}

de_results <- lapply(names(pseudobulk_list), function(ct) {
  run_limma_voom(pseudobulk_list[[ct]], ct)
})
names(de_results) <- names(pseudobulk_list)

de_all <- bind_rows(de_results)
```

### DE Summary

```{r}
#| label: de-summary
de_summary <- de_all |>
  group_by(cell_type) |>
  summarize(
    genes_tested = n(),
    up_FDR05   = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    down_FDR05 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05 & logFC < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    up_FDR10   = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.10 & logFC > 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    down_FDR10 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.10 & logFC < 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

DT::datatable(de_summary,
              caption = "Number of DE genes per cell type (VPA vs CTRL)",
              options = list(dom = "t"))
```

### Volcano Plots

Volcano plots show the relationship between effect size (log fold change, x-axis)
and statistical significance (−log10 adjusted p-value, y-axis). Genes in the
upper corners are both large in effect and statistically significant.

```{r}
#| label: volcano-plots
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 6
#| warning: false
volcano_plots <- lapply(names(de_results), function(ct) {
  df <- de_results[[ct]]
  df$sig <- ifelse(df$adj.P.Val < 0.05, "FDR < 0.05", "NS")

  # Top genes to label
  top_genes <- df |>
    dplyr::filter(adj.P.Val < 0.05) |>
    arrange(adj.P.Val) |>
    head(15)

  ggplot(df, aes(logFC, -log10(adj.P.Val), color = sig)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.8, alpha = 0.5) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("FDR < 0.05" = "red", "NS" = "grey60")) +
    geom_text_repel(
      data = top_genes,
      aes(label = gene),
      size = 3, max.overlaps = 20, color = "black"
    ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = -log10(0.05), linetype = "dashed", color = "blue") +
    labs(
      title = ct,
      x = "log2 Fold Change (VPA vs CTRL)",
      y = "-log10(adj. P-value)",
      color = NULL
    ) +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
})

wrap_plots(volcano_plots, nrow = 1)
```

### Heatmap of Top DE Genes

```{r}
#| label: de-heatmap
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 10
# Get top DE genes across all cell types
top_genes_for_heatmap <- de_all |>
  dplyr::filter(adj.P.Val < 0.10) |>
  group_by(cell_type) |>
  arrange(adj.P.Val) |>
  slice_head(n = 25) |>
  ungroup() |>
  pull(gene) |>
  unique()

if (length(top_genes_for_heatmap) > 2) {
  # Build a matrix of logFC values across pseudobulk samples
  # Use the averaged log-CPM from each pseudobulk
  heatmap_data <- list()
  for (ct in names(pseudobulk_list)) {
    pb <- pseudobulk_list[[ct]]
    y <- DGEList(counts = pb$counts, samples = pb$sample_info)
    y <- calcNormFactors(y)
    lcpm <- cpm(y, log = TRUE)
    genes_avail <- intersect(top_genes_for_heatmap, rownames(lcpm))
    if (length(genes_avail) > 0) {
      mat <- lcpm[genes_avail, , drop = FALSE]
      colnames(mat) <- paste0(ct, ":", colnames(mat))
      heatmap_data[[ct]] <- mat
    }
  }

  # Combine and scale
  all_genes <- Reduce(intersect, lapply(heatmap_data, rownames))
  if (length(all_genes) > 2) {
    hm_mat <- do.call(cbind, lapply(heatmap_data, function(m) m[all_genes, ]))
    hm_scaled <- t(scale(t(hm_mat)))

    # Annotation
    ann_col <- data.frame(
      condition = sub(".*:(CTRL|VPA)_.*", "\\1", colnames(hm_mat)),
      cell_type = sub(":.*", "", colnames(hm_mat)),
      row.names = colnames(hm_mat)
    )

    pheatmap(
      hm_scaled,
      annotation_col = ann_col,
      show_rownames = (nrow(hm_scaled) <= 50),
      cluster_cols = TRUE,
      cluster_rows = TRUE,
      main = "Top DE genes across pseudobulk samples (z-scored log-CPM)",
      fontsize_row = 7
    )
  } else {
    cat("Too few shared DE genes across cell types for a meaningful heatmap.\n")
  }
} else {
  cat("Fewer than 3 DE genes at FDR < 0.10; skipping heatmap.\n")
}
```


## Gene Set Enrichment Analysis

Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) asks whether genes belonging to known
biological pathways are systematically shifted up or down in expression. Rather
than testing one gene at a time, GSEA tests **sets of genes** that share a
function, making it more sensitive to coordinated but modest changes.

We rank genes by their limma t-statistic (which captures both effect size and
certainty) and test against **Hallmark** and **GO Biological Process** gene sets
from MSigDB.

```{r}
#| label: gsea-gene-sets
#| message: false
# Get gene sets
hallmark <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "H") |>
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol) |>
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)

gobp <- msigdbr(species = "Homo sapiens", category = "C5", subcategory = "GO:BP") |>
  select(gs_name, gene_symbol) |>
  split(x = .$gene_symbol, f = .$gs_name)

# Combine
all_gene_sets <- c(hallmark, gobp)
```

```{r}
#| label: gsea-run
#| message: false
#| warning: false
gsea_results <- lapply(names(de_results), function(ct) {
  df <- de_results[[ct]]
  # Create ranked list by t-statistic
  ranks <- setNames(df$t, df$gene)
  ranks <- sort(ranks, decreasing = TRUE)

  # Run fgsea
  res <- fgsea(
    pathways = all_gene_sets,
    stats = ranks,
    minSize = 15,
    maxSize = 500
  )
  res$cell_type <- ct
  res
})
names(gsea_results) <- names(de_results)

gsea_all <- bind_rows(gsea_results)
```

### Top Enriched Pathways

```{r}
#| label: gsea-dotplot
#| fig-width: 14
#| fig-height: 10
#| warning: false
# Top pathways per cell type (by adjusted p-value)
top_pathways <- gsea_all |>
  dplyr::filter(padj < 0.05) |>
  group_by(cell_type) |>
  arrange(padj) |>
  slice_head(n = 15) |>
  ungroup()

if (nrow(top_pathways) > 0) {
  # Clean names for display
  top_pathways$pathway_short <- gsub("^HALLMARK_|^GOBP_", "", top_pathways$pathway)
  top_pathways$pathway_short <- gsub("_", " ", top_pathways$pathway_short)
  top_pathways$pathway_short <- tolower(top_pathways$pathway_short)

  ggplot(top_pathways, aes(
    x = NES,
    y = reorder(pathway_short, NES),
    size = -log10(padj),
    color = NES
  )) +
    geom_point() +
    scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "grey80", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
    facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y") +
    labs(
      title = "Top enriched pathways (GSEA, padj < 0.05)",
      x = "Normalized Enrichment Score",
      y = NULL,
      size = "-log10(padj)",
      color = "NES"
    ) +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
} else {
  cat("No pathways reached significance at padj < 0.05.\n")
  # Show top pathways at a relaxed threshold
  top_pathways_relaxed <- gsea_all |>
    group_by(cell_type) |>
    arrange(pval) |>
    slice_head(n = 10) |>
    ungroup()

  if (nrow(top_pathways_relaxed) > 0) {
    top_pathways_relaxed$pathway_short <- gsub(
      "^HALLMARK_|^GOBP_", "", top_pathways_relaxed$pathway
    )
    top_pathways_relaxed$pathway_short <- gsub("_", " ", top_pathways_relaxed$pathway_short)
    top_pathways_relaxed$pathway_short <- tolower(top_pathways_relaxed$pathway_short)

    ggplot(top_pathways_relaxed, aes(
      x = NES,
      y = reorder(pathway_short, NES),
      size = -log10(pval),
      color = NES
    )) +
      geom_point() +
      scale_color_gradient2(low = "blue", mid = "grey80", high = "red", midpoint = 0) +
      facet_wrap(~cell_type, scales = "free_y") +
      labs(
        title = "Top pathways by nominal p-value (none reached padj < 0.05)",
        x = "Normalized Enrichment Score",
        y = NULL,
        size = "-log10(p-value)",
        color = "NES"
      ) +
      theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
  }
}
```

## Known Biology Check

We examine genes known to be responsive to VPA or involved in neural development
to see whether their expression patterns are consistent with expectations.

**Selected genes**:

- **HDAC targets / chromatin remodeling**: *HDAC1*, *HDAC2*, *HDAC3*, *EP300*, *CREBBP*
- **Neural progenitor markers**: *PAX6*, *SOX2*, *NES*, *HES1*, *NOTCH1*
- **Neuronal differentiation**: *DCX*, *TBR1*, *NEUROD1*, *NEUROD2*, *MAP2*
- **Cortical layer markers**: *SATB2*, *BCL11B* (CTIP2), *TLE4*
- **Apoptosis / cell stress**: *TP53*, *BCL2*, *BAX*

```{r}
#| label: known-genes-data
known_genes <- c(
  "HDAC1", "HDAC2", "HDAC3", "EP300", "CREBBP",
  "PAX6", "SOX2", "NES", "HES1", "NOTCH1",
  "DCX", "TBR1", "NEUROD1", "NEUROD2", "MAP2",
  "SATB2", "BCL11B", "TLE4",
  "TP53", "BCL2", "BAX"
)

# Filter to genes present in data
known_genes_present <- known_genes[known_genes %in% rownames(sce)]
cat("Genes present in dataset:", length(known_genes_present), "of", length(known_genes), "\n")
cat("Missing:", setdiff(known_genes, known_genes_present), "\n")
```

### Violin Plots

```{r}
#| label: known-genes-violin
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 14
#| warning: false
# Extract expression for known genes
if (length(known_genes_present) > 0) {
  expr_mat <- as.matrix(assay(sce, "X")[known_genes_present, , drop = FALSE])
  expr_df <- as.data.frame(t(expr_mat))
  expr_df$condition <- sce$condition
  expr_df$cell_type <- sce$cell_type

  expr_long <- expr_df |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = all_of(known_genes_present),
      names_to = "gene",
      values_to = "expression"
    )

  # Only plot for the 3 major cell types
  expr_long_major <- expr_long |>
    dplyr::filter(cell_type %in% cell_types_for_de)

  ggplot(expr_long_major, aes(condition, expression, fill = condition)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.7, linewidth = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = condition_colors) +
    facet_grid(gene ~ cell_type, scales = "free_y", switch = "y") +
    theme(
      strip.placement = "outside",
      strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, size = 8),
      strip.text.x = element_text(size = 9),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
    ) +
    labs(
      title = "Expression of known VPA-response and neural genes",
      x = NULL, y = "log1p expression", fill = "Condition"
    )
}
```

### Feature Plots (UMAP) for Top DE Genes

```{r}
#| label: feature-plots
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 12
#| warning: false
# Pick top DE genes across cell types
top_de_genes <- de_all |>
  dplyr::filter(adj.P.Val < 0.10) |>
  arrange(adj.P.Val) |>
  pull(gene) |>
  unique() |>
  head(8)

# If too few DE genes, use top by nominal p
if (length(top_de_genes) < 4) {
  top_de_genes <- de_all |>
    arrange(P.Value) |>
    pull(gene) |>
    unique() |>
    head(8)
}

if (length(top_de_genes) > 0) {
  # Extract expression
  expr_top <- as.matrix(assay(sce, "X")[top_de_genes, , drop = FALSE])
  umap_expr <- umap_df
  for (g in top_de_genes) {
    umap_expr[[g]] <- expr_top[g, ]
  }

  feature_plots <- lapply(top_de_genes, function(g) {
    ggplot(umap_expr[sample(nrow(umap_expr)), ], aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, color = .data[[g]])) +
      geom_point(size = 0.2, alpha = 0.5) +
      scale_color_viridis(option = "magma") +
      labs(title = g, color = "log1p\nexpr") +
      theme(legend.key.width = unit(0.5, "cm"))
  })

  wrap_plots(feature_plots, ncol = 4)
}
```


## Draft Results

```{r}
#| label: results-data
#| echo: false
n_cells <- ncol(sce)
n_ctrl <- sum(sce$condition == "CTRL")
n_vpa <- sum(sce$condition == "VPA")
n_donors <- length(unique(sce$donor_id))
n_cell_types <- length(unique(sce$cell_type))

# Composition changes
comp_summary <- comp_cond |>
  select(condition, cell_type, proportion) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = condition, values_from = proportion) |>
  mutate(change_pct = round((VPA - CTRL) * 100, 1))

# DE counts
n_de_005 <- sum(de_all$adj.P.Val < 0.05, na.rm = TRUE)
n_de_010 <- sum(de_all$adj.P.Val < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)

# Top pathway
top_pw <- gsea_all |> arrange(pval) |> head(1)
```

### Results Summary

We analyzed `r format(n_cells, big.mark = ",")` cells from
`r n_donors` donors across `r n_cell_types` cell types, comparing CTRL
(`r format(n_ctrl, big.mark = ",")` cells) to VPA-treated
(`r format(n_vpa, big.mark = ",")` cells) human dorsal forebrain organoids.

**Cell type composition**: VPA treatment was associated with notable shifts in
cell type proportions:

```{r}
#| label: results-comp-table
#| echo: false
DT::datatable(
  comp_summary |>
    mutate(
      CTRL = paste0(round(CTRL * 100, 1), "%"),
      VPA = paste0(round(VPA * 100, 1), "%"),
      `Change (pp)` = change_pct
    ) |>
    select(cell_type, CTRL, VPA, `Change (pp)`),
  caption = "Cell type proportion changes (percentage points)",
  options = list(dom = "t"),
  rownames = FALSE
)
```

**Differential expression**: Across the three major cell types tested,
we identified `r n_de_005` genes at FDR < 0.05 and `r n_de_010` genes at
FDR < 0.10.

**Pathway enrichment**: The top enriched pathway was
*`r gsub("_", " ", top_pw$pathway[1])`* in `r top_pw$cell_type[1]`
(NES = `r round(top_pw$NES[1], 2)`, nominal p = `r signif(top_pw$pval[1], 3)`).

**Limitations**: With only `r n_donors` donors per condition, these results
are exploratory. The use of back-transformed log1p data rather than raw counts
introduces approximation, though pseudobulk aggregation mitigates this.


## Draft Methods

### Data Source

Single-cell RNA-seq data were obtained from CELLxGENE
(dataset ID: `3a8aec06-3309-4d37-b75d-c59f5f6d55a6`), originating from
Yentür et al. (2025, bioRxiv). The dataset comprises human dorsal forebrain
organoids from `r n_donors` donors under control and VPA-treated conditions
(`r format(n_cells, big.mark = ",")` cells total).

### Preprocessing

Data were provided as log1p-normalized expression values. UMAP coordinates and
cell type annotations from the original authors were used without modification.

### Differential Expression

Pseudobulk expression profiles were generated by summing back-transformed
(expm1) approximate counts per gene across cells within each donor × condition
× cell type group. Differential expression was performed using the limma-voom
pipeline (Ritchie et al. 2015) with a paired design formula (~donor_id +
condition). Genes were filtered using `filterByExpr()`, library sizes
normalized with TMM (`calcNormFactors()`), and precision weights estimated
via `voom()`. Empirical Bayes moderation was applied with `eBayes()`.
P-values were adjusted for multiple testing using the Benjamini-Hochberg method.

### Pathway Analysis

Gene set enrichment analysis was performed using fgsea (Korotkevich et al. 2021)
with genes ranked by limma t-statistic. MSigDB Hallmark and GO Biological Process
gene sets were tested (gene set sizes 15–500).

### Software

```{r}
#| label: methods-software
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
pkgs <- c("R", "SingleCellExperiment", "edgeR", "limma", "fgsea", "msigdbr",
           "ggplot2", "plotly")
versions <- sapply(pkgs, function(p) {
  if (p == "R") {
    paste(R.version$major, R.version$minor, sep = ".")
  } else {
    as.character(packageVersion(p))
  }
})
cat(paste(
  paste0("**", pkgs, "** v", versions),
  collapse = ", "
), "\n")
```

+
+# Map Ensembl IDs to gene symbols where available
+# feature_name contains gene symbols for annotated genes, ENSG IDs otherwise
+gene_symbols <- as.character(rowData(sce)$feature_name)
+is_symbol <- !grepl("^ENSG", gene_symbols)
+
+# Make symbols unique (some may be duplicated)
+symbol_map <- gene_symbols
+symbol_map[is_symbol] <- make.unique(symbol_map[is_symbol])
+names(symbol_map) <- rownames(sce)
+
+# Create a lookup from ENSG to symbol
+ensg_to_symbol <- setNames(gene_symbols, rownames(sce))
+
+# Rename rows to gene symbols where available
+rownames(sce) <- symbol_map
